beats: Hook: one line of Python, backend="nccl", and a library sets off to survey the whole cluster before any data moves.
Survey: NCCL probes NVLink, PCIe and InfiniBand: wide fast roads inside a node, one narrow bridge between nodes.
Choice: a cost model picks ring or tree and a protocol from the layout and the message size; the data is cut into chunks streamed over several channels at once.
Toolbox: collectives (AllReduce, AllGather, ReduceScatter) for DP and TP, point-to-point Send/Recv for pipelines and MoE, group calls that bundle many operations into one launch.
Scale: at about 96k GPUs plain start-up takes ~265 s and failures force restarts; Meta's NCCLX starts in ~24 s.
Overlap idea: two jobs take max(t1, t2) instead of t1 + t2 when one runs during the other.

Why DP can overlap: backward runs from the last layer; layer i's AllReduce needs only layer i's gradients, so it runs while layer i-1 is computed: communication is off the critical path (washing and drying).
Numbers: overlap holds while bandwidth >= FLOPS x DP / (2 x tokens); bigger batches help, more DP hurts; TP and PP divide both sides, CP only the tokens.
Pitfall: when the drying is slower than the washing, the wet pile grows: at large DP the talk can no longer hide.
Cliffhanger: "any bugs in our analysis?": every GPU still carries a full copy of everything (into L05-02).
Cover (line_cover_l05_01; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): talking while working: two travellers chat as they wash and dry, plates flowing from the dirty stack to the clean rack.
